introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: Answer ALL the questions in the spaces provided (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: Answer ALL FOUR questions in this section; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.
incertitudes: Q B3 : barème imprimé par bloc ((i) 8 marks, (ii) 7 marks), rappelé dans l'énoncé de (c) et de (ii)(d). Les parties (i)(a)-(c) sont numérotées a à c et (ii)(a)-(d) numérotées d à g. Les tracés (triangles sur papier millimétré, construction à la règle et au compas) sont à faire par l'élève : le corrigé donne les coordonnées, la description du tracé et les valeurs à obtenir. Description complète de la transformation : rotation de 180 degrés (demi-tour) de centre l'origine, équivalente à une homothétie de centre O et de rapport -1. Diamètre du cercle inscrit : 7/racine(3) = 4,04 cm, soit 4,0 cm à la mesure (tolérance de mesure à relire par l'enseignant).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) On a graph paper and taking $1$ cm for $1$ unit on both axes.

(a) Draw triangle $PQR$ with coordinates $P(-1,4)$, $Q(-1,1)$ and $R(-4,1)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Draw the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis from $-5$ to $5$ with $1$ cm per unit.

Plot $P(-1,4)$, $Q(-1,1)$ and $R(-4,1)$, then join $P$ to $Q$, $Q$ to $R$ and $R$ to $P$.

Triangle $PQR$ has a right angle at $Q$ ($PQ$ is vertical, length $3$; $QR$ is horizontal, length $3$), so it is a right-angled isosceles triangle in the second quadrant.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Find the coordinates of the image $P'Q'R'$ of triangle $PQR$ under the transformation matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Multiply the matrix by the position vector of each point:

$P'$: $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-1\\4\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-4\end{pmatrix}$.

$Q'$: $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-1\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$.

$R'$: $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-4\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}$.

**$P'(1,-4)$, $Q'(1,-1)$, $R'(4,-1)$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Draw triangle $P'Q'R'$ and describe the transformation completely. *[8 marks for (i)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Plot $P'(1,-4)$, $Q'(1,-1)$, $R'(4,-1)$ on the same axes and join them: the triangle lies in the fourth quadrant.

Each image point is the original point with both coordinates changed in sign, $(x,y)\to(-x,-y)$.

**The transformation is a rotation through $180^\circ$ (a half-turn) about the origin $O(0,0)$.** (It is also an enlargement with centre $O$ and scale factor $-1$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Using a pencil, a ruler and a pair of compasses only.

(a) Construct triangle $ABC$ such that $AB=AC=BC=7$ cm.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Steps:

1. Draw $BC=7$ cm with the ruler.
2. With the compass set to $7$ cm and centre $B$, draw an arc above $BC$.
3. With the same radius and centre $C$, draw a second arc cutting the first at $A$.
4. Join $AB$ and $AC$.

Triangle $ABC$ is equilateral, with all sides $7$ cm and all angles $60^\circ$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Bisect any two angles in triangle $ABC$ and label the point $O$, where the bisectors meet.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Steps (for angle $B$, then repeat for angle $C$):

1. Centre $B$: draw an arc cutting $BA$ at $X$ and $BC$ at $Y$.
2. Keeping the same radius, centre $X$ and then centre $Y$: draw two arcs that cross inside the triangle.
3. Draw the line from $B$ through the crossing point: this is the bisector of angle $B$.
4. Do the same at $C$.

The two bisectors meet at the point $O$ inside the triangle (the third bisector, from $A$, passes through the same point).

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) With $O$ as centre, draw a circle such that $AB$, $AC$ and $BC$ are tangents to the circle.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Steps:

1. From $O$, construct the perpendicular to $BC$: with centre $O$ draw an arc cutting $BC$ twice, then bisect the part of $BC$ between the two cuts. The foot of the perpendicular is the point $T$ where the circle touches $BC$.
2. With centre $O$ and radius $OT$, draw the circle.

The circle touches the three sides $AB$, $AC$ and $BC$ (it is the inscribed circle, or incircle, of the triangle), because $O$ is at the same distance from the three sides.

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Measure and write down the length of the diameter of the circle. *[7 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The radius of the incircle of an equilateral triangle of side $7$ cm is the distance from $O$ to a side. The centre $O$ is also the centroid, so $OT=\dfrac13\times\text{height}$.

Height $=\sqrt{7^2-3.5^2}=\sqrt{36.75}\approx6.062$ cm, so the radius is $\dfrac{6.062}{3}\approx2.02$ cm.

Diameter $=2\times2.02\approx4.04$ cm.

**Measured diameter $\approx4.0$ cm** (exact value $\dfrac{7}{\sqrt3}\approx4.04$ cm).
